entries.claim: `readArtifact` follows artifact symlinks without checking that the resolved target remains below the planning root, so a phase directory that passed `phaseDirsIn`'s directory-level containment guard can still cause reads outside that root.
entries.failure_scenario: In an untrusted repository, create a valid `.planning/phases/1/` with a conforming plan and make `SUMMARY.md` a symlink to an outside regular file containing a `## Commits` table. A `/cad-why` invocation reads it, indexes its rows, and renders its Description cell into both `text` and `entries`; a similarly linked adjudication JSON can place arbitrary `claim`, `failure_scenario`, and `counter_evidence` bytes in the output envelope. The regular-file check only rejects devices/FIFOs after resolution; it does not confine the resolved regular file.

entries.claim: The regular-file check is vulnerable to a check-to-use race: the path can be replaced with a FIFO after `statSync` reports a regular file and before `readFileSync` opens it.
entries.failure_scenario: A concurrent process replaces `SUMMARY.md` or a matching `ADJUDICATION-*.json` with a FIFO immediately after line 94. `readFileSync` then opens the FIFO and blocks waiting for a writer, hanging `/cad-why` rather than producing the documented fail-open warning. This defeats the stated guard against FIFO reads.

counter_evidence.note: The race is real in principle but its exploitable half is the same defect as finding 0 and is closed by the same fix: b5f49bad refuses a path whose realpath leaves the directory it was joined onto, so a swapped-in symlink cannot point outside after the check. What remains is an actor with local write access inside .planning/phases/<N>/ swapping a regular file for a FIFO in the same directory, whose consequence is a hang on the user own machine by someone who could already write arbitrary planning bytes. High overstated on that residue; ruled low and queued as an open item.

entries.claim: Untrusted adjudication records are parsed with no input-size or structural-depth limit after their entire contents have already been synchronously loaded.
entries.failure_scenario: A repository can add a multi-gigabyte regular `ADJUDICATION-*.json` file in a resolved phase. `readArtifact` loads it wholly into memory and `JSON.parse` allocates the parsed representation synchronously; `/cad-why` can exhaust memory or stall before its parse-error handling is reached. A valid JSON value padded with a huge string or deeply nested arrays avoids the malformed-JSON catch while causing the same availability failure.

counter_evidence.note: The observation is true - JSON.parse at why-record.mjs:477 caps neither size nor depth. The premise is not: an ADJUDICATION-*.json is Cadence own artifact, written by planning.mjs adjudication into the user own .planning/, not third-party input, and every other JSON read in this tree (config.mjs, planning.mjs trace and cursor reads) is unbounded the same way, so a cap here alone would be an approach difference rather than a closed hole. The consequence is memory spent reading a file the caller already owns. High overstated; ruled low and queued as an open item.
